data.title: C3is Earnings Call Highlights Growth, Cash and Fleet Expansion
data.description:
C3is Inc. ((CISS)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

C3is delivered a strongly positive message on its earnings call, highlighting sharp growth in revenue, profit, cash, fleet capacity and charter rates. The main setbacks were third-quarter losses tied to dry-docking, a non-cash warrant loss and continued geopolitical disruption across shipping routes.

Revenue Growth Accelerates

Voyage revenue surged 249% to $16.7 million in the third quarter of 2026, from $4.8 million a year earlier. For the first nine months, revenue rose 116% to $52.4 million, reflecting the impact of a larger fleet and stronger markets.

Nine-Month Profitability Improves

Net income for the first nine months reached nearly $12 million, up 128% from $5.3 million in the prior-year period. Adjusted net income climbed 1,300% to $13.2 million, compared with an adjusted loss of $1.1 million in 2025.

Net Revenue and Operating Income Rise

Third-quarter net revenue increased 209% year over year to $9.3 million, while nine-month net revenue rose 148% to $36.7 million. Nine-month operating income reached $12.8 million, compared with a $1.2 million operating loss in 2025.

EBITDA Expands Sharply

Management reported strong EBITDA growth for the first nine months, although the call cited differing figures of $17.8 million and $78.8 million. Adjusted EBITDA was reported at $19 million, up 387% from $3.9 million, underscoring improved vessel earnings and operating leverage.

Cash Position Strengthens

Cash stood at $59.7 million at the end of September, up 300% from year-end 2025. By mid-November, cash had increased further to $64.9 million, giving C3is greater flexibility to fund vessel obligations and pursue growth.

Cash Covers Product-Tanker CapEx

C3is said its cash balance amply covers the $39.7 million to $39.78 million obligation for two recently acquired product tankers. The payment is due in January 2027, but management indicated that the commitment does not require bank financing.

Balance Sheet Remains Debt-Free

The company reported no bank debt despite expanding fleet capacity by 387% since inception. Shareholders’ equity rose 29% to $122.7 million at the end of the third quarter, compared with $95.1 million at year-end 2025.

Fleet Expands and Diversifies

C3is took delivery of the Clean Fury and Clean Reaper product tankers during the second and third quarters. At quarter-end, the fleet comprised three Handysize bulk carriers, one Aframax tanker and two product tankers, with total capacity of 311,000 deadweight tons.

Tanker and Fleet Rates Improve

The Aframax tanker’s third-quarter time charter equivalent rate jumped 595% year over year to $81,300. Fleetwide TCE increased 136% to $20,900, showing the benefit of stronger tanker pricing and broader fleet exposure.

Bulk Carrier Charters Secured

The company agreed to time charter two bulk carriers at $19,500 per day, with contracts ending in December 2026 and March 2027. A third bulk carrier was fixed at $17,000 per day through January 2027, providing near-term revenue visibility.

Fleet Avoids Chinese-Built Vessel Risk

Management said none of C3is’s vessels were built in China. As a result, the fleet is not expected to face potential U.S. tariffs or elevated port fees aimed at Chinese-built ships.

Product Tanker Exposure Grows

The two acquisitions increased C3is’s exposure to the product tanker market, which management described as healthy. Disrupted Middle East refining flows, shifting refining advantages toward the Atlantic Basin and inventory restocking were cited as supportive factors.

Dry Bulk Market Shows Strength

Management called the third quarter a superb period for dry bulk shipping, with the Baltic Dry Index averaging above 3,000. That was the strongest quarterly average since the COVID-driven boom of 2021, while bauxite flows through September rose 20% year over year.

Broad Commodity Demand Supports Shipping

C3is pointed to urbanization, infrastructure spending, electric vehicle production and renewable-energy installations as long-term demand drivers. Saudi Vision 2030, industrial expansion and demand for iron ore, steel, coal, grains and minor bulks were also cited, along with longer routes that raise ton-mile demand.

Vessel Quality Remains a Priority

All vessels have ballast water treatment systems and are unencumbered, according to management. The fleet operates through short- to medium-term charters and spot voyages, while regular inspections and a comprehensive maintenance program support vessel quality.

Charterer Relationships Strengthen

The management company said it has built strategic relationships and repeat business with international charterers. Customer loyalty was attributed to safety and reliability, with vessels chartered to commodity traders, industrial companies, oil producers and refineries.

Growth Strategy Stays Disciplined

C3is said it is combining technical and condition assessments with selective purchases of quality, non-Chinese-built vessels. The company is also using equity issuances and focusing on short- to medium-term charters and spot voyages to balance growth with flexibility.

Third-Quarter Adjusted Loss Narrows

C3is recorded a third-quarter adjusted net loss of $2.1 million, narrower than the $3.4 million loss a year earlier. Management said the result was mainly affected by two dry-docking projects rather than a deterioration in underlying vessel demand.

Operating Loss Reflects Dry Docking

The company reported a third-quarter operating loss of $2 million, compared with a $3.5 million loss in the prior-year quarter. The result primarily reflected dry-docking costs for one product tanker and one bulk carrier.

Dry-Docking Costs Weigh on Results

Three vessels underwent dry docking during the first nine months of 2026. The work cost $4.5 million for the nine-month period, including $3.1 million in the third quarter, temporarily reducing reported earnings.

Warrant Loss Was Non-Cash

C3is recorded a $1.1 million unrealized loss on warrants during the first nine months. Management emphasized that the charge was non-cash and did not reflect the company’s operating performance or vessel-level earnings.

Geopolitical Risks Remain Elevated

Management cited attacks on trade routes, tankers, ports and pipelines, including tensions involving Iran, the Houthis, Saudi Arabia and the Black Sea. Disruption around the Strait of Hormuz also contributed to energy-price concerns by reducing inventories and increasing fears of renewed conflict.

Trade Routes Face Ongoing Uncertainty

The call highlighted port congestion, canal diversions, slower steaming and possible disruption around the Panama Canal. Uncertainty also remains over Middle East refining flows, attacks on Russian refineries, Arabian Gulf trade and the reopening of pipelines.

Related-Party Payables Detailed

Payables to a related party totaled $42.4 million, primarily reflecting the $39.78 million balance for the Clean Fury and Clean Reaper tankers. A further $2.6 million was owed to the management company, although management said that amount had already been paid.

Guidance Points to Continued Growth

Management said it will continue using equity issuances to pursue timely, selective acquisitions of quality non-Chinese-built vessels, while maintaining a focus on short- to medium-term charters and spot voyages. It also said the $39.78 million January 2027 tanker payment is covered by cash and expressed confidence in repeating its strong performance in the fourth quarter.

C3is ended the call with a favorable growth story built on stronger markets, a larger fleet and ample cash. Dry-docking costs, geopolitical risk and market uncertainty remain important watch points, but the debt-free balance sheet and improving earnings provide a solid foundation for expansion.

data.title: Terra Innovatum Earnings Call Signals Reactor Progress
data.description:
Terra Innovatum Global N.V. ((NKLR)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Terra Innovatum’s earnings call carried a predominantly positive tone, with management pointing to funded equipment orders, successful testing, completed NRC readiness materials and progress at the Rock City site. However, the company still faces important hurdles, including nonbinding customer opportunities, unfinished licensing and construction milestones, a projected 2027 cash burn of $30 million to $35 million and the possibility of raising additional capital for commercialization.

Deployment Plan Moves Toward Execution

Terra Innovatum said it is moving from preparation toward execution as equipment procurement, manufacturing planning and customer discussions advance together. The company continues to target its first-of-a-kind SOLO reactor in 2027 and commercial deployments from 2028, subject to regulatory approvals and project milestones.

Major Equipment Orders Are Funded

The company signed a procurement agreement with Turboden for steam turbine and generator equipment. After the quarter ended, Terra made down payments for graphite components from Mersen, turbine equipment from Turboden and an air-cooled condenser from SPG Dry Cooling.

Manufacturing Readiness Improves

Terra advanced assembly planning and manufacturing procedures while evaluating dedicated factory space with ATB Riva Calzoni. The effort is designed to support the first reactor and create repeatable production processes for future units.

Helium Circulator Passes Hot Test

A helium circulator using the design planned for SOLO completed a four-hour hot running test successfully. Terra was also acquiring two additional helium blowers for nonnuclear system testing and interface evaluations.

All 18 Draft PSAR Chapters Shared

Terra completed the delivery of all 18 draft preliminary safety analysis report chapters to the NRC for readiness review. Management described the work as a substantial engineering and safety-analysis milestone beyond the initial package of nine chapters and an environmental report.

Regulatory Review Remains on Track

Management said it had seen no event likely to delay the construction permit application. The second readiness-review phase is expected to begin after the current phase, which management expects to complete before year-end, while the construction permit target remains the second half of 2027.

Waiken Deal Opens International Opportunity

Terra signed a nonbinding letter of intent with Waiken ILW covering potential deployment of up to 8 megawatts electric of behind-the-meter SOLO capacity. The proposed projects would support DIRECTV Latin America and SKY Brasil data-center infrastructure in Argentina and Brazil.

Commercial Frameworks Become More Detailed

The company is developing framework agreements covering reactor quantities, schedules, responsibilities, payment terms and possible reservation deposits. Management said these agreements are intended to move qualified opportunities toward definitive reactor purchase contracts.

First-of-a-Kind Budget Tracks Plan

Terra said it had spent about one-third of its $70 million first-of-a-kind budget for 2026 and 2027. Management expects the program to finish on budget and retain between $20 million and $30 million for commercialization efforts.

Cost Estimates Remain Stable

Management said procurement costs remain aligned with estimates made about 18 months earlier. Expected minor plant-layout changes are not viewed as affecting prior forecasts, and the estimated cost of the first commercial reactor remains consistent with projections made two years ago.

Outsourced Model Limits Overhead

Terra plans to rely on existing suppliers and manufacturing capabilities rather than vertically integrating its supply chain. Management said this approach should keep overhead low, with no expected supply-chain integration during the first commercialization phase through roughly 2030 or 2031.

Third-Quarter Profit Included Noncash Gain

Terra reported third-quarter net income of $61 million, or $0.55 per basic and diluted share. The result included $67.5 million of noncash gains related to changes in the fair value of settled contingent warrant liabilities.

Operating Expenses and Supplier Advances

Third-quarter operating expenses totaled $7.1 million, including $1.7 million of development costs and $5.4 million of general and administrative expenses. Advances to suppliers under SOLO development agreements stood at $2.6 million on September 30.

Rock City Site Work Begins

Terra began work at Rock City on Admiral Parkway, including boreholes and soil analysis. Management said recent soil results were positive and that the site is covered by the construction permit rather than requiring a separate site permit.

Fuel Procurement Advances

The company submitted fuel specifications to its vendor and is actively finalizing procurement. Management said the required amount of low-enriched uranium fuel is readily producible by the current industry.

Customer Deposits Could Support Funding

Terra is working on customer frameworks that could include down payments of 25% to 30% of the estimated reactor cost. Such deposits would provide early funding and signal stronger customer commitment once agreements become binding.

Cash Balance Declines in the Quarter

Cash and cash equivalents fell to $82.4 million at September 30, 2026, from $91.1 million three months earlier. Management said the timing of supplier payments and equipment deliveries will cause quarterly cash usage to vary.

Waiken Opportunity Is Still Nonbinding

The potential 8-megawatt Waiken deployment remains a letter of intent rather than a firm order. Terra must convert this and other LOIs or MOUs into binding reactor purchase agreements and executable deployment plans.

Licensing and Construction Milestones Remain Open

Management stressed that completing the 18 draft PSAR chapters does not represent NRC approval or acceptance of a formal application. Terra still must address NRC feedback, continue readiness-review work, advance the construction permit application and prepare its operating-license application.

Equipment and Fuel Work Continues

Several major equipment packages remain under discussion, while fuel procurement has not yet been completed. EPC work is underway at Rock City, but the company continues to organize site engineering and construction activities.

2027 Cash Burn Expected at $30 Million to $35 Million

Terra expects cash burn of $30 million to $35 million in 2027. Management said most of the spending will support supplier payments tied to equipment deliveries.

Additional Capital May Be Needed

Management said Terra has enough cash to complete the first-of-a-kind reactor. However, the company may need to raise additional capital after that phase to fund commercialization and supplier advance payments under firm contracts.

Customer Confidence Is the Main Bottleneck

Management identified customer confidence and purchase commitments as the main commercial challenge. Prospective customers want protection against delays and greater pricing certainty while Terra works through licensing, first-of-a-kind execution and binding orders.

First Reactor Is Central to Commercialization

Terra views completion of the first-of-a-kind reactor at Rock City, or the reactor vessel at ATB, as a key commercial turning point. Demonstrating that the design works could help change customer behavior and support stronger purchase commitments.

Part 57 Timing Has Shifted

Management said Part 57 is now expected to become effective in February 2027. Terra is assessing whether to continue under Part 50 while potentially beginning a Part 57 commercial licensing process in parallel.

Forward Guidance

Terra continues to target first-of-a-kind deployment in 2027, a construction permit in the second half of 2027 and commercial deployments beginning in 2028. The company expects to remain within its $70 million first-of-a-kind budget, spend about $15 million on regulatory work, retain $20 million to $30 million for commercialization and pursue customer deposits of 25% to 30% of reactor costs.

Key Takeaways

Terra Innovatum’s call showed clear progress from planning toward funded procurement, regulatory preparation and site execution. The investment case still depends on completing licensing, proving the first reactor and converting nonbinding customer interest into firm orders, while cash needs and potential future financing remain important risks.

data.title: NRx Pharmaceuticals Earnings Call Signals Commercial Turnaround
data.description:
Nrx Pharmaceuticals, Inc. ((NRXP)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

NRx Pharmaceuticals’ earnings call carried a predominantly positive tone as management highlighted the company’s shift from development stage to commercial operations. FDA approval, a first customer order, higher patient revenue, nearly $20 million in cash and four business divisions were balanced by operating losses, dilution concerns and regulatory, clinical and market uncertainties.

First FDA Approval Marks Key Milestone

NRx said the FDA approved its abbreviated new drug application for preservative-free ketamine on October 29, 2026. The company called it its first drug approval and the first approval of a blow-fill-seal Luer-Lock vial as a drug-device combination.

Commercial Launch Begins With First Order

The company has deployed a 17-person veteran sales force and received its first order for preservative-free ketamine during the quarter. Management presented the order as an early sign that NRx is moving from development toward commercial execution.

Cash Improves as Convertible Debt Falls Away

NRx ended the third quarter with about $19.8 million in cash and cash equivalents, compared with $7.8 million at the end of 2025. The company said it has eliminated convertible debt, while a public offering generated more than $22 million in gross proceeds.

Patient Revenue Shows Strong Growth

Net patient revenue rose to $1.2 million in the third quarter from $0.2 million a year earlier. The increase reflects growing activity at HOPE Therapeutics and provides an early commercial revenue stream for the broader business.

Nine-Month Net Loss Narrows

NRx reported a nine-month net loss of $20.1 million, down from $29 million in the comparable 2025 period. The improvement was mainly tied to fair-value accounting changes and nonrecurring convertible-note and restructuring charges recorded in the prior year.

Ketamine Market Offers Significant Opportunity

Management estimates annual U.S. demand for sterile injectable ketamine at roughly $400 million, with growth above 17%. It said several additional sterile products could double or triple NRx’s addressable market, while the wider generic sterile-products market is estimated at $23 billion.

Blow-Fill-Seal Process Could Lower Costs

NRx said its manufacturing process can produce 900,000 blow-fill-seal units in the time needed to package 50,000 glass bottles. Expected cost of goods is about $0.75 per unit, compared with approximately $3.25 for glass packaging.

Packaging Targets Hospital Efficiency

The Luer-Lock vial is designed to avoid sharps waste and reduce handling steps compared with traditional glass containers. NRx cited strong user satisfaction and time savings in human-factor studies, against a backdrop of about 385,000 annual sharps injuries among U.S. hospital personnel.

NRX-100 Moves Toward FDA Submission

NRx plans to submit a rolling new drug application for NRX-100 by the end of 2026 and believes approval could come in 2027 through a regular or accelerated route. The regular filing is expected to include data from more than 500 randomized-trial patients and 65,000 patients represented by real-world evidence.

Yale and PCORI Support Ketamine Study

NRx signed a collaboration agreement with Yale University and joined, with PCORI approval, a study comparing intravenous ketamine with intranasal S-ketamine. The company said the research is intended to provide confirmatory evidence for an accelerated-approval pathway.

DARPA Funds NRX-101 Trial

DARPA awarded NRx Defense Systems an initial $11.2 million prime contract for the Phase 2/3 SPARC-TMS trial of NRX-101 with robotic transcranial magnetic stimulation. The study is expected to enroll and treat more than 400 patients, with results planned after the treatment period.

Defense Division Reaches Early Milestones

NRx Defense Systems satisfied its initial DARPA milestones, and its first two invoices were approved for payment in the fourth quarter. Management said the division is expected to rely on nondilutive funding, reach profitability and provide a modest contribution to the parent company.

HOPE Expands Its Technology Focus

HOPE Therapeutics generated its first clinical revenue in the fourth quarter of 2025 and operated six Florida locations as of September 30, 2026. Its partnership with Zeta Surgical has brought robotic neuronavigated TMS into the network, with the first patients already treated.

NRX-200 Advances as Subcutaneous Program

NRx developed a neutral-pH ketamine formulation using an FDA-approved cyclodextrin vehicle exclusively licensed to the company. The formulation has demonstrated feasibility and is being prepared for additional development work.

NRX-101 Shows Product Readiness

NRX-101 has FDA breakthrough therapy designation and has shown reductions in depression, suicidality and akathisia. NRx said the treatment outperformed lurasidone in two randomized trials for akathisia and suicidality, while drug and placebo supplies for the DARPA trial are ready.

GeNeuro Adds ALS and Schizophrenia Potential

GeNeuro is pursuing disease-modifying approaches for ALS and schizophrenia through programs including GNK-301 and Temelimab. NRx cited research linking HERV-K envelope protein to many ALS cases at the National Institutes of Health and said preclinical work showed GNK-301 blocked related toxic effects.

GeNeuro Science Day Planned

NRx plans to hold a GeNeuro Science Day during the first week of December 2026. The event is expected to explain the division’s scientific findings and development opportunities to investors and other stakeholders.

Four Divisions Shape Corporate Strategy

NRx operates NeuroRx Pharmaceuticals, HOPE Therapeutics, NRx Defense Systems and GeNeuro. Management said each division is intended to use financing structures that may limit dilution and has an opportunity to become profitable independently.

Operating Losses Remain a Concern

Loss from operations increased to $8.1 million in the third quarter from $4 million in the prior quarter. For the first nine months, operating loss reached $19.4 million, compared with $11.6 million a year earlier, as clinic costs, research spending and commercial-launch expenses rose.

Quarterly Net Loss Improves Year Over Year

NRx reported a third-quarter net loss of $2.2 million, or $0.05 per share, compared with $5.9 million, or $0.27 per share, in the prior-year quarter. The result shows improvement in reported net loss despite continued investment in expansion and product development.

Shareholder Dilution Remains Sensitive

Management acknowledged that investors have been concerned about dilution over the past two years. Although the recent offering strengthened the balance sheet, NRx said it may use its active at-the-market facility opportunistically.

NRX-100 Approval Still Depends on FDA Review

The NRX-100 application has not yet been submitted, and NRx is discussing scientific questions with the FDA, including comparability between the MADRS and PHQ-9 depression scales. The company is pursuing regular and accelerated routes, but approval remains subject to regulatory review.

Ketamine Safety and Market Access Need Resolution

NRx said chronic intravenous ketamine use remains an open question because of possible addiction and neurotoxicity risks. It also cautioned that a market-clearing event tied to its citizen petition is not assured and that broad supply capability must be demonstrated.

Manufacturing Advantage Is Not Exclusive

Competitors could adopt a similar blow-fill-seal approach, although NRx believes they would need equipment, engineering and validation work, plus two years of stability data. The company does not have exclusive rights to Rommelag blow-fill-seal machines.

HOPE Drops Clinic Roll-Up Strategy

NRx originally expected to borrow money and lead a clinic roll-up, but management said it saw roll-up strategies failing across the country. HOPE has instead shifted toward technology, including robotic TMS and other tools intended to support its clinical network.

Biotechnology Market Remains Challenging

Management described equity-market conditions for biotechnology companies as difficult. That environment could make fundraising more expensive or increase pressure on companies such as NRx to demonstrate commercial progress.

Forward Guidance Points to 2027 Commercial Goals

NRx aims to demonstrate a path to profitability in 2027 while funding innovation through nondilutive sources where possible. The company expects NRX-200 pharmacokinetic testing in early 2027, a first-in-human study in September 2027 and more than 400 SPARC-TMS patients treated during 2027, while targeting NRX-100 approval in 2027 and estimating a $400 million ketamine market that could expand with additional products.

NRx’s call presented a company with meaningful commercial and regulatory milestones, but one that is still spending heavily and relying on successful execution. FDA progress, revenue growth, manufacturing economics and potential nondilutive funding support the bullish case, while losses, dilution, competition and approval uncertainty remain important risks for investors.

data.title: Horizon Kinetics Earnings Call Highlights Growth Amid Volatility
data.description:
Horizon Kinetics Holding Corporation ((HKHC)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Horizon Kinetics Holding Corporation’s earnings call carried a broadly optimistic tone, with management emphasizing its investment pipeline, private-company relationships, real-asset strategy and operating improvements. That confidence was tempered by a 40% drop in operating income, an $18.4 million shareholder loss, higher expenses, lower sequential revenue and limited near-term incentive fee accruals.

Technology and Operational Improvements

Management said improved use of technology is giving the company clearer organization-wide visibility and smoother communication between departments. Faster workflows, fewer silos and stronger internal coordination are producing what executives described as great strides in daily operations.

Broader Investment Opportunity Network

The company said its private and public investment opportunities have never been better. A growing network of relationships is producing almost too many attractive opportunities to evaluate, underscoring management’s confidence in the long-term investment pipeline.

ETF Marketing Campaign Begins

Horizon Kinetics has launched its first formal marketing campaign for its exchange-traded funds, initially focusing on the inflation-beneficiary INFL ETF. Management said the ETF group is profitable overall, while smaller unprofitable products have not previously received a fair marketing opportunity.

INFL Leads ETF Revenue Growth

INFL revenue rose 26% in the quarter from a year earlier and 30% year to date compared with 2025. The fund’s assets were recently around $1.5 billion to $1.6 billion, and management said it had recorded inflows in the preceding months.

Royalty and Real-Asset Funds Gain Momentum

Recent marketing efforts for the royalty and real-asset funds have attracted a meaningful amount of new money, according to management. The company expects the product to surpass $100 million within the next few months, possibly by early 2027 or sooner.

ReFlow Targets Mutual Fund Liquidity

Horizon Kinetics has begun using ReFlow, which allows mutual funds to obtain liquidity by transferring securities in kind rather than selling individual holdings. Management said the structure should make mutual funds more similar to ETFs in recognizing gains and could reduce taxable gains during future rebalancing.

Product Rationalization Underway

The company is reviewing strategies that appear too similar and may confuse investors in the marketplace. Management plans to exit lower-margin products and consolidate offerings into strategies with stronger economics and clearer positioning.

Buyback and Dividend Announced

The board authorized a $25 million share repurchase program for opportunistic purchases beginning after the earnings call. It also declared a $0.13 per share dividend payable December 10, 2026, bringing trailing 12-month dividend declarations to $0.507 per share.

Direct Relationships Expand Private Portfolio

Management highlighted direct relationships with operators and investments in LandBridge, WaterBridge, WhiteHawk and PBT Land and Minerals. The company has also invested in roughly 18 other private businesses for itself and advisory clients that co-invest through private vehicles.

Evergreen Capital for Private Investments

The company described its private investment product as an evergreen series designed to provide very long-term, stable capital. Management also expects clients to receive additional opportunities to invest alongside Horizon Kinetics in selected private companies.

Focus on Scarce Hard Assets

Horizon Kinetics said its strategy centers on hard assets tied to artificial intelligence development and electrification, including natural gas, water and strategically located land. Management stressed that these assets can be profitable without further data-center construction, while additional development provides upside optionality.

Natural Gas Opportunity Highlighted

Management contrasted U.S. natural gas prices of roughly $3 with prices near $17 in Europe and $13 in Asia. It said existing projects could multiply U.S. export capacity, potentially lifting liquefied natural gas exports from about 15% to 40% of domestic supply, while noting that prices have historically reached three or four times current levels.

Portfolios Show Differentiated Behavior

Management said its portfolios have been up when the broader market was down and down when the market was up in nearly half of the months reviewed over the past year or two. Executives presented this pattern as evidence that the portfolios behave differently from major market benchmarks.

Western Texas Asset Position

Peter Doyle described the company as having created a horizontal monopoly in western Texas. Horizon Kinetics owns toll roads and businesses connected with the region’s emerging water, land, power and data-center opportunities.

Advisory Revenue Remains Stable Year Over Year

Third-quarter advisory revenue was $17.8 million, essentially flat compared with the same quarter of 2025. The stability provided a measure of support for the core advisory business despite weaker sequential results and pressure in mutual fund revenue.

Year-to-Date Advisory Fees Rise

Management advisory fees totaled $77.9 million for the nine months ended September 30, up 27% from $61.2 million a year earlier. The figure included an $18.1 million first-quarter performance incentive fee tied to the expiration of trading restrictions on Miami International Holdings investments.

Positive Nine-Month GAAP Results

For the first nine months, Horizon Kinetics reported GAAP net income of $35.8 million, or $1.92 per share. Results reflected steady operating income from the core asset-management business and investment gains that occurred primarily during the first quarter.

Strong Liquidity and No Third-Party Debt

At September 30, the company held $36.4 million in cash, an $86 million investment portfolio, $12 million in digital assets and about $243 million invested in private funds. It had no third-party debt, with long-term liabilities limited mainly to office-space leases.

AUM Remains Above Year-End Level

Assets under management stood at $10 billion on September 30, above the $9.6 billion recorded at December 31, 2025. However, the figure was below the $10.8 billion reported in the second quarter, reflecting market-value swings in several major holdings.

Bitcoin-Linked Holdings Rebound During Quarter

The company’s holdings connected to Bitcoin-linked securities rose 43% during the quarter. Despite that improvement, they remained down 6% for the year, highlighting the volatility affecting investment-related results.

Sequential Advisory Revenue Declines

Although third-quarter advisory revenue was unchanged from the prior-year period at $17.8 million, it fell 5.3% sequentially. The decline points to softer near-term momentum even as management continues to emphasize longer-term growth opportunities.

Operating Income Falls 40%

Third-quarter operating income dropped 40% from a year earlier to $1.8 million. Management attributed much of the decline to a $0.8 million right-of-use impairment and duplicative costs from replacing the company’s New York City office.

Operating Expenses Increase

Third-quarter operating expenses rose $1.3 million year over year to $16.3 million. The company said duplicative office costs and the right-of-use impairment had a meaningful effect on the quarter’s expense base.

Quarterly Net Loss Reported

Horizon Kinetics reported a quarterly net loss of $59 million, including $41 million attributable to redeemable noncontrolling interests in consolidated investment products. The loss attributable to HKHC shareholders was $18.4 million, or $0.98 per share.

Mutual Fund Declines Offset ETF Growth

Growth from the ETF group, led by INFL, was largely offset by lower revenue from mutual funds. The mixed product performance shows that ETF momentum has not yet translated into broad-based revenue growth across the company’s investment offerings.

AUM Falls as TPL and Bitcoin Assets Swing

AUM declined from $10.8 billion in the second quarter to $10 billion at September 30. Management attributed the change mainly to fair-value movements in Texas Pacific Land and Bitcoin-linked securities; TPL fell 25% during the quarter but remained up 13% year to date.

Limited Near-Term Incentive Fees

The company had approximately $6.9 million of unearned incentive fees tied to existing private funds at September 30. About $6.7 million involved investments that could face additional liquidity restrictions, and management said fourth-quarter incentive fee revenue was unlikely to be significant and could remain volatile.

Mutual Funds Face Capital Gains Distribution

Various funds are expected to distribute capital gains in the near future. Management characterized the Paradigm Fund’s distribution as fairly large and said ReFlow had not been in place during 2026 to reduce its size.

ETF Campaign Results Not Yet Measurable

The formal ETF marketing effort had only just begun, so management did not yet have measurable results attributable to the campaign. Executives also clarified that recent INFL inflows were not linked to a direct marketing push.

Unrealized Gains Add Earnings Volatility

Management warned that GAAP net income can be heavily affected by unrealized gains and losses on investments, including digital assets. Results may also vary from quarter to quarter and year to year because of the company’s incentive fee structure.

Underlying Advisory Fees Edge Lower

Year-to-date advisory fees totaled $54.8 million before the separately presented $18.1 million first-quarter incentive fee. Excluding that incentive fee, the figure was down 1.2% from 2025, indicating modest pressure beneath the headline year-to-date growth rate.

Forward-Looking Guidance

Management said the royalty and real-asset fund could exceed $100 million within the next few months, while INFL was recently around $1.5 billion to $1.6 billion and its marketing campaign had just begun. ReFlow is expected to reduce mutual fund gains, fourth-quarter incentive fees are not expected to be significant, and the company cited an approximately $80 million revenue run rate, a $25 million buyback and substantial long-term investment potential.

Overall, the call paired near-term earnings pressure with strong confidence in Horizon Kinetics’ investment platform and asset strategy. The company is dealing with expense increases, volatile marks and softer mutual fund revenue, but management sees meaningful opportunities in ETFs, private investments, natural gas, water and land while maintaining liquidity and shareholder distributions.

data.title: Kandi Technologies Earnings Call Signals Profitable Growth
data.description:
Kandi Technologies ((KNDI)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Kandi Technologies delivered a broadly positive earnings call, highlighted by strong revenue growth, a return to operating and net profitability, improving liquidity, and progress in battery swapping. The company also pointed to expanding North American channels and planned product launches, although lower margins, higher costs, and inventory clearance remained important challenges.

Revenue Growth Accelerates

Kandi’s net revenue for the first nine months of 2026 reached $82.1 million, up 38.5% from $59.3 million a year earlier. Management attributed the increase mainly to stronger off-road vehicle sales and revenue contributed by Rawrr.

Off-Road Business Expands

Revenue from Kandi’s core off-road electric vehicle business rose 33.5% to $74 million. Rawrr contributed $18 million to that total, strengthening the company’s position in electric recreational vehicles.

Operating Profit Returns

Kandi reported income from operations of $0.8 million for the first nine months of 2026, compared with an operating loss of $5.8 million in the prior-year period. The improvement reflects stronger sales and lower operating expenses.

Net Profitability Restored

Net income reached $5.6 million, reversing a $6.3 million loss in the same period of 2025. Basic and diluted net income attributable to shareholders was $0.58 per share, compared with a loss of $0.55 per share previously.

Liquidity Position Strengthens

Cash, restricted cash, and certificates of deposit totaled $291.3 million at September 30, 2026, up from $211.9 million at the end of 2025. Working capital stood at $190.8 million, giving Kandi significant financial resources for expansion.

Battery Swapping Begins Producing Revenue

Kandi’s battery swapping equipment business began contributing revenue in the third quarter. Management described the milestone as further evidence that the business is moving from development toward commercialization.

CATL Subsidiary Places Orders

China Battery Exchange secured four orders from QIJI Energy, a CATL subsidiary, during the third quarter. The orders cover 33 heavy-duty truck battery swapping stations and provide an important commercial reference for the business.

Equipment Production Moves Forward

Kandi organized production in four batches during the quarter, with 32 heavy-duty truck battery swapping units entering production. Manufacturing was completed for 17 units, while 11 were installed and delivered at customer sites.

Battery Capacity Expansion Continues

Renovation and production ramp-up at China Battery Exchange’s new manufacturing facility are progressing in phases. The first renovated area began operating on September 5, and Kandi is targeting capacity of 36 units per month in 2027.

Strategic Cooperation With CATL Deepens

Kandi continued expanding its strategic cooperation with CATL while developing battery swapping equipment. The work includes improving production, delivery capabilities, product quality, and customer service.

North American Retail Access Broadens

Kandi established a partnership with a leading North American home improvement retailer, and its UTV products began entering the retailer’s sales channel. The agreement could improve consumer access and support brand visibility in a major market.

Dealer Network Keeps Expanding

The company continued to enlarge its North American dealer network and optimize its sales channels. Management said a more diversified channel mix should improve market coverage and make sales efforts more efficient.

Golf Cart and UTV Portfolio Refreshed

Kandi is refining its golf cart and UTV lineup as it transitions the brand to a refreshed product offering. The company is also upgrading existing products to better match changing customer preferences and market demand.

Rawrr Product Development Advances

Kandi is using its research, manufacturing, supply chain, and distribution resources to support Rawrr’s electric off-road motorcycle business. Management said new Rawrr products are progressing well and will expand the company’s off-road product range.

Operating Expenses Decline

Total operating expenses fell 5.7% to $30.9 million from $32.8 million in the first nine months of 2025. The reduction helped Kandi return to operating profitability despite pressure from a changing product mix.

Marketing Spending Falls

Selling and marketing expenses dropped 34.3% to $7.2 million from $11 million. Kandi attributed the savings mainly to lower advertising costs following changes to its marketing approach and distribution channels.

Investment Strategy Remains Broad

Management plans to continue strengthening the off-road electric vehicle business and commercializing battery swapping equipment. It is also pursuing backup power and energy storage opportunities for artificial intelligence data centers, overseas expansion, and improved capital efficiency.

Gross Margin Comes Under Pressure

Gross margin declined to 38.6% from 45.5% a year earlier. Kandi said the decrease mainly reflected changes in product mix and the relatively lower gross margin generated by Rawrr products.

Cost of Goods Sold Rises Faster

Cost of goods sold increased 56% to $50.4 million from $32.3 million, largely because of higher sales. The faster increase than revenue was a key reason profit growth lagged the company’s top-line expansion.

General and Administrative Costs Increase

General and administrative expenses rose 9.5% to $19.7 million from $18 million. The increase partially offset savings in selling and marketing expenses and remains an area for management to monitor.

Research Spending Edges Higher

Research and development expenses increased 4.2% to $4 million from $3.9 million. The spending supports Kandi’s product upgrades, Rawrr development, and broader electric vehicle and energy initiatives.

Inventory Clearance Remains a Priority

Kandi is working to clear slow-selling models and non-new vehicles from its inventory. The effort is intended to improve product turnover and make room for newer offerings, though it may continue to affect pricing and margins in the near term.

Gross Profit Trails Revenue Growth

Gross profit rose 17.6% to $31.7 million from $26.9 million, well below the pace of revenue growth. Management linked the difference to product mix changes and the lower margins associated with Rawrr sales.

Forward-Looking Guidance

Kandi expects renovation of the remaining main production area at China Battery Exchange’s facility to finish in the next couple of weeks, with capacity targeted at 36 units per month in 2027. Slow-selling inventory clearance and golf cart and UTV upgrades are targeted for completion in the fourth quarter of 2026, while new Kandi products and Rawrr products are scheduled to launch in phases beginning in the first quarter of 2027.

Kandi’s earnings call presented a company making meaningful progress toward profitable growth and commercialization of battery swapping. Strong liquidity, expanding channels, and new products support the outlook, but margin pressure, rising costs, and inventory cleanup remain important risks for investors.

data.title: Infratil Earnings Call Signals Strong Growth Ahead
data.description:
Infratil Limited ((NZ:IFT)) has held its Q2 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Infratil’s earnings call struck a strongly positive tone, with management highlighting 28% growth in proportionate EBITDAF, higher guidance, stronger liquidity and continued dividend growth. Challenges included higher interest rates, weaker healthcare and Qscan results, lower Wellington Airport traffic and timing risks around contracts, projects and the Qscan sale, but the overall message remained confident.

Strong First-Half Performance and Raised Guidance

Management called the first half strong and lifted FY2027 proportionate operational EBITDAF guidance to $1.37 billion-$1.44 billion. That compares with the previous range of $1.32 billion-$1.42 billion, raising the lower end by $50 million and the upper end by $20 million.

Proportionate EBITDAF Increased 28%

Proportionate operational EBITDAF reached $711 million, up $156 million, or 28%, from the prior period. CDC contributed $105 million of the increase, One NZ added $29 million and Longroad contributed $15 million.

CDC and Longroad Delivered Contracted Capacity

CDC added 90 megawatts of billing customer capacity and increased its guidance, while Longroad completed 600 megawatts of new capacity. All of Longroad’s completed projects were contracted when built, and revenue from them contributed during the half.

Contracted Growth Drove Higher Capital Investment

Proportionate capital expenditure almost doubled to $2.1 billion, mainly because of CDC and Longroad construction programs. Management said strong customer demand pulled spending forward and that the investment is being directed toward contracted growth.

Portfolio Asset Value Increased

Infratil’s total portfolio asset value rose 8% to $22.3 billion, or about $17.94 per share after management fees. The value was 10% higher than in March, with CDC the largest contributor after adding $2.4 billion.

Dividend Growth Continued

Infratil declared a half-year dividend of $0.074 per share, an increase of 2.1% from the prior period. The dividend included $0.012 of imputation credits, preserving the company’s track record of dividend growth.

CDC Maintained Strong Credit and Funding Position

More than 90% of CDC customers are investment grade or higher, supported by long lease terms. CDC has raised more than $4 billion for its construction program, including $1.4 billion since September, with average funding costs targeted at about 6%.

CDC Construction Program Tracking to Plan

CDC has spent slightly less than 20% of planned capital expenditure for the 810 megawatts under construction. Development milestones, including the first tranche of Building 1 at Laverton in Melbourne, are progressing, while cost control supported a $20 million increase at both ends of its annual guidance range.

Strong CDC Demand and Pipeline

Management said demand remains very strong across several customer segments and that CDC is well placed to win further contracts as capacity becomes available. Large blocks are expected to come online from 2029, while the company continues to expand its development pipeline.

Longroad Advanced Its Renewable Development Program

Longroad remains on track to begin construction on 1.6 gigawatts of projects during the year. The Utah Notch Peak solar project is underway, while its 2.8-gigawatt Amargosa project moved closer to regulatory approvals and represents most of the 3.1-gigawatt contracted backlog from 2027 onward.

Longroad Capacity Expansion Target Maintained

Longroad retained its target of doubling operating capacity to 14 gigawatts by the end of 2029. Management said its data-centre strategy remains prospective and that progress toward it is satisfactory.

One NZ Delivered EBITDAF Growth and Brand Progress

One NZ EBITDAF rose by $29 million in the first half, with mobile performance strengthening in higher-value and mobile virtual network operator segments. The One NZ brand ranked first in consideration among noncustomers, which management described as an important indicator of future trading performance.

One NZ Transformation and Fibre Initiatives Progressed

One NZ’s major information-technology transformation remains on track, with an intellectual-property sale for its new network platform validating the work’s quality. EonFibre also progressed well, its trans-Tasman high-bandwidth service launched and a previously announced hyperscaler contract remained on track.

One NZ Guidance Was Narrowed and Maintained

One NZ narrowed FY2027 EBITDAF guidance to $610 million-$640 million and capital expenditure guidance to $240 million-$260 million. Annual distributions are expected to remain consistent with FY2026, while the company’s medium-term targets were unchanged.

Wellington Airport Resilient Despite Lower Passenger Numbers

Wellington Airport EBITDAF was broadly flat and its margin held at 73%, despite passenger numbers falling about 8%. Commercial execution and disciplined cost control offset most of the decline, allowing FY2027 EBITDAF guidance to remain at $130 million-$140 million.

Kao Data Reached 99% Contracted Capacity

Kao Data’s portfolio is now 99% contracted, representing about 55 megawatts of capacity. The London KLON-03 site is expected to add 17.6 megawatts from early 2027, while greenfield developments in Manchester and West London progressed into early works and customer discussions.

Healthcare Businesses Made Operational Progress

Infratil’s New Zealand diagnostic-imaging business began benefiting from its performance-improvement program. Qscan won a large hospital contract in Brisbane that is expected to be onboarded by the end of the financial year, while Anytime Radiology is operating and winning additional revenue.

Liquidity and Leverage Improved

Available liquidity increased to $1.4 billion from $1.1 billion in March, while net debt stood at $3.1 billion. The loan-to-value ratio declined to 14.2% from 15.4%, and Infratil retained its S&P BBB+ stable rating.

Capital Expenditure Guidance Increased for Faster Development

Proportionate FY2027 capital expenditure guidance rose to $4.15 billion-$4.45 billion, mainly because CDC development activity accelerated. Management stressed that the increase reflected faster development rather than higher project costs.

Sustainability Performance Improved

Infratil continued to improve its GRESB sustainability scores, including a perfect score for Wellington Airport. The company also released its FY2026 environmental, social and governance data book.

Cash-Flow Self-Sufficiency Metric Was Achieved

Infratil achieved its cash-flow self-sufficiency metric for the first half, helped by higher distributions from portfolio companies. Management expects CDC distributions to provide increasing support for the medium-term objective.

Statutory Net Parent Loss

Infratil recorded a statutory net parent loss of $248 million, including a $256 million accounting provision for incentive fees linked to CDC’s higher equity valuation. Management said the final fee will depend on year-end valuations and that a prior-year negative accrual will provide an offset.

Higher Interest Rates Pressured Valuations

Higher risk-free rates and a steeper forward yield curve offset part of the portfolio’s valuation gains. Management described interest rates as one of the largest headwinds for businesses that rely on contracted revenue.

Longroad Valuation Declined

Longroad’s underlying value fell by US$198 million during the period, mainly because an 80-basis-point rise in base rates increased project discount rates. Progress on its refreshed development plan and further Infratil investment reduced the net valuation decline to $39 million.

Qscan Valuation and Trading Performance Weakened

Qscan’s valuation declined by $91 million, reflecting a $46 million distribution received in April, a higher valuation discount rate and recent trading performance. Earnings were slightly below the prior year as solid revenue was offset by cost pressures.

One NZ EBITDAF Included Nonrecurring Benefits

Of One NZ’s $29 million EBITDAF increase, $20 million came from a nonrecurring intellectual-property sale and cost-timing benefits recorded in the first half. Management also noted inflationary pressure and legacy cost escalation, although operating expenses were flat.

Wellington Airport Passenger Numbers Declined

Passenger numbers at Wellington Airport fell about 8%, largely because airlines reduced capacity in response to higher aviation fuel prices. Management is concentrating on cost control and working with airlines to help restore capacity.

Kao Data Result Was Flat During Revenue Ramp-Up

Kao Data’s half-year result was flat because mobilisation and operating costs ran ahead of the expected revenue ramp-up. The business is carrying a highly contracted portfolio and is progressing additional sites.

New Zealand Healthcare Earnings Remained Flat

New Zealand healthcare earnings were flat despite progress under the performance-improvement program. Guidance was maintained, although management said the business was tracking toward the lower half of its range as the program continues.

Qscan Earnings Declined Due to Cost Pressures

Qscan earnings were slightly lower than a year earlier, as good revenue growth was outweighed by cost pressures. Management said the team is addressing the issue while working to improve operational performance.

Qscan Sale Process Will Take Longer

Qscan was described as a high-quality business with strong buyer interest, but the potential sale is expected to take longer. The company is working through recent cost pressures and incorporating the new Brisbane hospital contract before progressing further.

Renewable Development Returns Outside the U.S. Lagged

Development returns outside the United States have lagged those available in the U.S. In response, Gurīn and Galileo are focusing on fewer, larger projects aimed at the end of the decade, while Gurīn’s Vanda project remains stalled pending Indonesia-Singapore discussions.

CDC Contracting and Development Timing Remain Uncertain

CDC continues to discuss additional contracts, although management cautioned that timing is difficult to predict. Kemps Creek and Gregadoo remain development projects without secured outcomes or confirmed grid connections, while about 250 megawatts of excess operating and construction capacity has taken longer than expected to contract.

Longroad Faces Near-Term Financial-Close Timing Risk

About 700 megawatts of Longroad projects still needed to reach financial close by year-end. Management remained confident because all but one had signed power-purchase agreements, but said the final project could slip by one or two months.

Regulatory and Funding-Market Uncertainty Remain

Management cited higher regulatory requirements, more selective lenders and recent funding-market volatility as industry challenges. It also said the pace of artificial-intelligence adoption and near-term data-centre forecasts remain variable.

Forward-Looking Guidance

Infratil raised FY2027 proportionate operational EBITDAF guidance to $1.37 billion-$1.44 billion and capital expenditure guidance to $4.15 billion-$4.45 billion, with CDC lifted to A$730 million-A$770 million. One NZ expects EBITDAF of $610 million-$640 million and capital expenditure of $240 million-$260 million, Wellington Airport remains at $130 million-$140 million, and Qscan was reduced to $75 million-$85 million.

Overall Takeaway

The call showed an expanding portfolio led by CDC, Longroad and One NZ, with stronger earnings, investment and liquidity supporting a positive outlook. Interest rates, operating costs, healthcare weakness and project timing remain risks, while full-year cash-flow self-sufficiency may fall slightly below target despite a strong first half.

data.title: Argosy Property Earnings Call Shows Stronger Leasing Momentum
data.description:
Argosy Property ((NZ:ARG)) has held its Q2 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Argosy Property’s earnings call struck a positive but measured tone, with management pointing to stronger leasing, high tenant retention, successful asset sales and a lower level of debt. Those gains were tempered by weaker net profit, valuation pressure, higher incentives, excess industrial supply and expectations for further interest-rate increases.

More Positive Outlook and Leasing Progress

Management said its outlook was more positive than at the previous update, supported by encouraging leasing progress over the past six months. The company believes this momentum is strengthening Argosy’s position for the future, despite continued pressure in parts of the property market.

Property Sales Near or Above Book Value

The Warehouse in Taupo sold for $11.4 million, which was 8.6% above its September book value. Foundry Drive in Christchurch was under contract at around book value, while Argosy continued work on its 99 Khyber Pass property.

Share Buyback Under Consideration

Argosy said its comfortable debt position, restricted development pipeline, asset sales and large discount to asset backing support consideration of a share buyback. Management added that a buyback would not necessarily prevent the company from pursuing other desirable opportunities.

Stable Dividend and Distributable Income

Net distributable income increased despite a marginal decline in property income, while the dividend remained unchanged at $0.0665 per share. Argosy declared a second-quarter dividend of $0.016625 per share, payable on December 23.

Occupancy and Lease Duration Improve

Occupancy recovered to its usual trend, with 147 Lambton Quay almost 80% leased following a transaction completed after the reporting period. The weighted average lease term rose to about 5.6 years, while executed leases yet to begin generating rent represent more than $6.7 million in annualized income.

Tenant Retention Remains High

Tenant retention exceeded 90%, highlighting the stability of Argosy’s customer base. Leasing and sales activity also continued through the domestic election without the usual slowdown, with 15 leases completed during the period and further transactions completed afterward.

Flight to Quality and Green Buildings

Management said tenants are increasingly seeking high-quality, well-located, environmentally responsible and seismically resilient buildings. More than 80% of leasing demand outside retail is specifically for green space, a trend that has supported activity at 147 Lambton Quay.

Gross Property Income Edges Higher

Gross property income rose to $69.7 million from $69.4 million in the comparable period. Rent reviews helped, with 61 reviews delivering a 2.9% annualized increase, while the acquisition of 291 East Tamaki Road and completed developments also contributed.

Insurance Costs Continue to Fall

Argosy reported further insurance savings, including a 19% reduction from the renewal effective October 1, 2026. About $400,000 of the saving is expected to flow through to the company’s bottom line in coming periods.

Tax Expense Falls on Mount Richmond Deduction

Current tax expense declined to $2.9 million from $6.1 million, helped by an investment boost deduction following completion of Warehouse 6 at Mount Richmond. The tax-effected value of the deduction was $2.1 million.

Balance Sheet Strengthens

Debt as a percentage of total assets fell to 36.6% at September 30 from 37.2% in March. The Taupo sale is expected to lower gearing by another 0.3%, and management described the balance sheet as remaining in very good shape.

Green Financing to Reduce Costs

Argosy refinanced its ARG020 green bond with bank debt, extended and trimmed its bank facilities, and converted $700 million into green loans under a new framework. The arrangement is expected to reduce margins and line fees by $2 million a year from November 2026.

Mount Richmond Development Completed

The Mount Richmond development was completed on time and on budget, supporting the company’s execution record. Viatris is reportedly very happy with its new space, while the remainder of the site is leased as hardstand.

Longer Lease Commitments Secured

Cardinal leases at Puhinui Road were extended across three properties by six years each, moving their expiry dates to 2040. Argosy also completed the Neilson Street lease to ECLY, while work linked to a Mayo Road transaction is expected to generate additional rent.

Retail Demand Remains Positive

Large-format retail continues to be a solid, location-dependent sector for Argosy. The company reported improved demand and good rental growth at Albany Mega Centre, providing support while other property segments face more uncertainty.

Net Property Income Declines

Net property income fell to $60.6 million from $61.2 million, while net property expenses rose by $950,000. Insurance savings were outweighed by higher Wellington rates and water costs, the absence of a prior-period rebate and expenses on vacant space, particularly at Neilson Street.

Net Interest Expense Increases

Net interest expense rose to $20.9 million from $18.8 million. A positive rate variance was offset by higher average debt levels and $1.9 million of lower capitalized interest than in the prior comparable period.

Net Profit Falls Sharply

Net profit after tax, including revaluation gains and losses, declined to $16.2 million from $61.1 million. The comparison reflects property valuation pressure as well as the broader impact of higher expenses and financing costs.

Per-Share Distributable Income Softens

Gross distributable income decreased to $33.9 million from $36.8 million, while net distributable income per share slipped to $0.0356 from $0.0358. The payout ratio increased to 90% from 88%, even though the dividend itself remained steady.

FFO Per Share Declines

Funds from operations was broadly flat at $32.2 million. However, FFO per share fell to $0.0369 from $0.0377, reflecting the effect of a larger share base on returns to individual shareholders.

Valuation Uncertainty Persists

Argosy recorded an internally assessed revaluation provision of $18.1 million, while the value of investment properties fell by $6 million from March. Management said valuers are facing limited market evidence and noted that the growing gap between green and non-green assets is not captured in broad market statistics.

Industrial Market Faces Excess Supply

The Auckland industrial market continues to carry significant excess stock, while demand has been slower. Management said industrial yields could soften further, net effective rents have eased slightly and current rental levels make new development difficult to justify.

Development Pipeline Remains Restricted

Argosy said its development pipeline is likely to remain constrained for the next 24 months. The company is not planning further development at Mount Richmond, and its development team has halved in size over the past six months.

Leasing Incentives Rise

Leasing incentives have increased to about 20% as tenants remain unwilling to fund their own fit-outs, contributing to a small decline in net effective rents. The Neilson Street lease included a 12% incentive, with the tenant paying half rent for the applicable period.

Bond Yields and Rates Add Pressure

Long-term bond yields remain elevated, with the greatest impact being felt in the industrial sector. Management also expects interest rates to continue rising, citing a broad market expectation of a 3.5% increase in the official cash rate.

Acquisitions and Asset Sales Face Constraints

Management said acquisitions would be challenging given the smaller development pipeline and current market conditions. The 147 Lambton Quay asset remains on the sale list, but strong leasing activity has made it more productive to retain for now, while 99 Khyber Pass is not expected to sell before Christmas.

Forward Guidance

Argosy does not expect to undertake development activity, with the pipeline likely to remain constrained for the next 24 months because current rental levels do not support new projects. Leasing inquiry remains strong, while management expects interest rates to rise and says more than 80% of non-retail demand is for green space.

Management expects the FY27 expiry at 17 Mayo Road to be replaced by a new 10-year lease, with negotiations for Visypet well advanced and the tenant expected to stay. Foundry Drive is expected to become unconditional immediately before Christmas, while 99 Khyber Pass could return to the market in the first calendar quarter of next year.

Argosy’s earnings call presented a company with improving leasing momentum, strong tenant retention and a healthier balance sheet, even as profit and per-share measures weakened. The key investor watchpoints are property valuations, industrial oversupply, interest rates and whether asset sales or a buyback can unlock value.

data.title: Bank of Georgia Earnings Call Signals Strong Growth
data.description:
Bank of Georgia Group Plc ((GB:BGEO)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Bank of Georgia’s earnings call carried a strongly positive tone, with record digital engagement, rapid loan and deposit growth, rising profits and stronger returns. Improving efficiency, healthy capital and liquidity, and continued shareholder distributions outweighed concerns over inflation, normalized credit costs, Armenian real estate and Russia-related exposure.

Digital Banking Reaches Record Scale

Georgia’s monthly active retail app users rose almost 14% to more than 2 million, while over 1 million customers open the app each day. In Armenia, monthly active users jumped nearly 37% to 417,000, with daily users growing even faster.

Customer Satisfaction and Digital Recognition Improve

Georgia’s net promoter score reached a record 78%, while retail and business app satisfaction stood at about 92% and 93%, respectively. Global Finance named the group the World’s Best AI Bank and World’s Best Consumer Digital Bank, following two years as the World’s Best Digital Bank.

Loans and Deposits Expand Rapidly

Group loans grew almost 25% and deposits increased 21% on a constant-currency basis, exceeding the company’s medium-term 15% benchmark. Growth came alongside stable or slightly higher net interest margins, supporting both revenue and profitability.

Revenue Growth Drives Efficiency

Combined revenue increased 19.6% year over year, while costs rose only 9%, lifting pre-provision growth to about 25%. The group recorded its lowest-ever cost-to-income ratio at 32.1% in the third quarter, showing the benefit of positive operating leverage.

Georgia Delivers Strong Profit Growth

Georgia’s quarterly profit rose 13.9% to GEL 494 million, while nine-month profit climbed 13.7% to GEL 1.4 billion. The Georgian loan book expanded 18.6% in constant currency and deposits grew 14.5%, maintaining strong momentum in the core market.

Digital Channels Dominate Georgian Lending

Georgia counted up to 2 million monthly digital users and 1.08 million daily users. Digital channels originated 87% of loans, while monthly active business users reached 117,000, underlining the bank’s broad digital reach.

Payments Gain Share in Georgia

Georgian acquiring volume and payment transactions increased 23.1% year over year and 14.3% from the prior quarter. Market share reached 56.8%, active merchants rose 15.9% to nearly 30,000 terminals, and issuing and payment users increased 12.5% to 1.7 million.

Capital and Liquidity Remain Robust

Georgia held capital buffers of 2.6 percentage points over CET1 requirements, 3.1 points over Tier 1 and 2 points over total capital requirements. Liquidity coverage reached 150%, compared with a 100% minimum, while the net stable funding ratio stood at 132%.

Ameriabank Adds Significant Profit Momentum

Ameriabank’s profit rose almost 45% year over year, or more than 30% excluding one-off effects from the prior quarter. Return on equity reached 24.4%, above the group’s medium-term guidance, while loans grew more than 38% and deposits nearly 40% in constant currency.

Armenia Expands Its Digital and Payments Franchise

Ameriabank’s monthly active customers reached about 600,000, up 25%, while digital monthly users increased 36.8% and daily users grew faster. Acquiring activity rose more than 22%, issuing activity nearly 50%, and the bank became Armenia’s market leader in issuing business volume.

Ameriabank Strengthens Market Position

Ameriabank lifted its loan market share to 23% and increased retail term-deposit share by 0.9 percentage points, reinforcing its leadership in retail time deposits. Capital buffers were about 140 to 150 basis points above regulatory requirements, with liquidity coverage above 200% and a net stable funding ratio of 125%.

Group Returns and Fee Income Accelerate

Group revenue grew just under 20%, net interest income rose 19.4%, and post-provision growth reached 21% after pre-provision growth of 25%. Return on equity was 27.2% and return on assets was just below 4%, while fee income rose strongly in both markets after adjusting for prior Mastercard-related effects.

Automation Supports Operating Leverage

Management said automation and artificial intelligence are being deployed in transaction processing, anti-money-laundering controls and chatbot and call-center operations. These initiatives are expected to create cost savings over time and could also support revenue, although they require continued investment in staff and technology.

Shareholder Returns and Book Value Rise

Nine-month capital distributions increased 17.6%, while the third-quarter dividend rose 23.6% year over year. The group is currently returning about 20% of earnings through dividends and about 10% through buybacks, while book value per share increased 31.5% in dollar terms.

Economic Backdrop Remains Supportive

Management described growth in Georgia and Armenia as resilient, supported by diversified external inflows, stronger connectivity and major investment projects. Record international reserves, appreciating currencies and contained public debt and fiscal deficits were cited as signs of macroeconomic stability.

Investment Projects Create Lending Opportunities

Large-scale projects in both countries are strengthening trade and regional connectivity, creating new corporate lending opportunities. In Armenia, management pointed to mining investments and major data centers developed with NVIDIA as examples of activity supporting credit demand.

Asset Quality Remains Controlled

Group cost of credit was 68 basis points in the quarter, while non-performing loans and coverage remained healthy and NPLs stayed near historical lows. Management said higher Georgian credit costs reflected the end of favorable expected-credit-loss adjustments rather than a deterioration in underlying asset quality.

Funding Is Diverse and Stable

Both banks were described as having very strong liquidity, supported by long-term funding from institutions including EBRD, FMO, DEG and DFC. Ameriabank also has excess local-currency liquidity that can support additional retail lending, while the group’s funding base was described as diversified and countercyclical.

Inflation and External Risks Remain

Food and fuel prices continue to keep inflation elevated in Georgia and Armenia, prompting central banks to maintain tight monetary policy; Armenia recently raised its policy rate to 7%. Management also highlighted Armenia’s wider current-account deficit, although capital inflows and foreign investment were viewed as sufficient to support reserves.

Armenian Real Estate and Russia Exposure Monitored

Ameriabank said mortgage risk remains moderate because of loan-to-value levels, primary-market concentration and a tax-rebate program, although the central bank has warned of possible real estate overheating. Indirect Russia-related exposure is limited to the high single digits of the loan book, but a sharp deterioration there could still affect trade, energy costs and results.

Deposit Mix and M&A Strategy Remain Disciplined

Georgia deliberately reduced some corporate deposits to remain below a 40% market-share threshold that could trigger additional capital charges. Management also said M&A remains under review, but valuations have made value-accretive deals difficult, so any transaction would need to strengthen the group and focus on selected systemic banks.

Forward Guidance and Capital Policy

Management maintained its 2026 GDP growth forecasts of 7.5% for Georgia and 5.5% for Armenia, with next year’s growth expected at 5.5% to 6%. Medium-term loan growth is expected to settle near 10% in Georgia and 20% in Armenia, blending to about 15%; cost-to-income below 35% is viewed as healthy, while Armenia’s cost of risk is expected to fall toward 1% to 1.2% and its margin could improve toward roughly 6.3%. Capital distributions remain targeted at 30% to 50% of earnings, with dividends and buybacks currently accounting for about 20% and 10%, respectively.

Overall, Bank of Georgia presented a picture of strong growth, high digital adoption and improving efficiency across both markets. Risks around inflation, credit-cost normalization, Armenian property and Russia exposure remain, but robust capital, liquidity, customer engagement and shareholder returns leave the group well positioned.
